header.lead: The question isn’t whether AI can read a data room. It’s what has to happen before a finding reaches you.

difference.title: Engineered every time versus steered on the day
difference.lead: A pipeline someone has already built, run and hardened is a different thing from assembling that same rigor yourself, under deal pressure, once.

pipeline.title: From upload to a finding you can act on
pipeline.lead: From upload to drafted findings, the analysis runs with no human in the loop. One mandatory human gate sits after it.

stages.title: Grounded retrieval
stages.body: Each module is an independent agent that retrieves evidence from the uploaded documents.
stages.note: Confidential financial and personal data is pseudonymized before it reaches this layer.

stages.title: Drafting against the schema
stages.body: Findings are drafted inside a schema that requires a citation for every claim.

stages.title: Generate-critique-retry
stages.body: A second reviewer agent critiques the draft and sends it back. The loop repeats.
stages.note: The platform’s own term for it: a generate-critique-retry loop.

stages.title: Independent fact-check
stages.body: An independent pass cross-verifies claims against the source text.
stages.note: A third checking layer, distinct from both the reviewer agent and the human gate.

stages.title: Cross-discipline reconciliation
stages.body: Every discipline’s findings are checked against every other’s and resolved into one narrative.

stages.title: Human review and approval
stages.body: A named person reviews already-generated findings before release. This is what makes machine-speed analysis safe to rely on.
stages.note: Pseudonymization is reversed only here, in the final delivered output.

refusals.title: Three things the loop will not auto-approve
refusals.lead: Three failure classes are hard-coded to route to a person, even after repeated retries.

classes.title: Fabricated or hallucinated source citations

classes.title: Privacy leaks
classes.body: Anything that shouldn’t have crossed into or out of the analysis layer goes to a person.

classes.title: Scope refusals
classes.body: Where a module can’t answer within its brief, it says so and escalates.

limits.title: What we don’t claim about the platform
limits.lead: Everything on this page describes a mechanism. None of it is a certified metric.
items: No accuracy rate. Internal benchmarks are single-dataset and unaudited.
No claim that the human gate is optional. It is mandatory.
No completed public case studies yet.
No uniform track record. The financial module has run end to end on a live deal and been verified against source documents. The reconciliation layer is younger.
No general availability. Factum is pre-launch.

items.q: Isn’t this just an AI chatbot with extra steps?
items.a: The difference isn’t AI versus no AI. It’s a tested pipeline versus a session someone steers under deal pressure. Every discipline runs its own pre-scoped pass, every time, and the cross-check between them is a fixed step.

items.q: How do I know the platform can carry findings this material?
items.a: The financial module is the most numerically exposed part of any read. It has run end to end on a live deal and been independently verified against source documents. Newer layers have less history, and we tell you which is which.

items.q: What happens when the model doesn’t know?
items.a: It has to say so. A finding is either backed by a real citation or flagged as unconfirmed. An unresolvable citation is one of the three classes the reviewer loop refuses to auto-approve.

items.q: Who is accountable for what reaches me?
items.a: A named person, who reviews every output before it leaves.
The pipeline pass runs in hours. The finished, reviewed output takes days. We don’t quote a delivery date before seeing the data room.

faq.title: The ones that come up first

items.q: Does this replace a quality-of-earnings report?
items.a: It is broader, and it is not an attest service. A quality-of-earnings read covers one dimension in four to ten weeks. This runs eleven disciplines and reconciles them. A signed accountant’s opinion stays a separate engagement.
Days, not weeks. The pipeline pass runs in hours; human review and reconciliation come after it. We don’t commit to a date before seeing the data room.
One price for the whole scope, set on the intake call against the size and state of your data room. No tiered menu.

Confidential data is pseudonymized before analysis and reversed only in the final output. Analysis runs on Google Vertex AI in an EU region under a Data Processing Agreement. The model provider does not keep your documents or train on them.

items.q: Can I see an example report?
items.a: Not a real one. Client documents are confidential and no client has elected to be named. On a call we can show you the live dashboard, the output schema, and how a finding traces back to its source.
A named person, before anything reaches your desk. While Factum is pre-launch, that person is the founder, on every mandate.

header.title: How your documents are handled, and what we don’t claim
header.lead: Data handling is built into how the pipeline runs. It is also narrower than most security pages imply, so this page states the boundary.

data.title: Four things that are true of every engagement
data.lead: Each one describes a mechanism in the pipeline. None of them is a certification.

gate.title: The one mandatory human step
gate.lead: The analysis runs without a human in the loop. The gate sits after it, and it is not optional.
items: Findings are checked back against the source documents before delivery.
The gate runs every time, automatically.
Three failure classes route to a person instead of auto-approving: fabricated citations, privacy leaks, and scope refusals.
A named person reviews, reconciles and stands behind the output.
Pseudonymized values are reversed only here, in the final output.

transparency.title: Where the machine ends and a person starts
transparency.lead: You should be able to tell, for any finding, what produced it and what checked it.
steps: Independent agents retrieve evidence from your uploaded documents.
A second reviewer agent critiques each draft.
A separate pass fact-checks claims against the source text.
Claims that can’t be tied to a passage are flagged as unconfirmed.

limits.title: What we don’t claim
limits.lead: Most of what a buyer wants on a page like this, we don’t have yet. Listing it beats implying it.
items: No ISO 27001, SOC 2 or any other certification. No third-party audit of the pipeline.
No penetration test, sub-processor list, single sign-on or audit-log commitment.
No published EU region. Analysis runs on Google Vertex AI in an EU region; we don’t name which one.
No retention or deletion period on Factum’s own side. Zero retention is the model provider’s commitment.
No asserted GDPR-compliance status. Processing terms belong in an engagement agreement.
No professional-indemnity cover, breach-notification or disaster-recovery commitment stated here.
limits.note: If your process needs any of these in writing, raise it on the intake call. There is a real answer either way.

boundaries.title: What a partnership does not include
boundaries.lead: Some are commitments to existing partners. The rest is the honest state of a pre-launch company.
items: No white-labelled claim of certification or audit. We can’t stand behind a badge we don’t hold.
No unlimited capacity. A partnership that outruns the review gate is worse than no partnership.
No blanket referral-fee policy. Where attest or independence rules apply, it is checked per relationship.
No claim on your client. Nothing we run for you becomes a case study without your written agreement.
No conflicting mandate where we have already committed exclusively. Where an exclusivity exists, we say so.

items.q: Do you work directly with owners as well?
items.a: Yes. Where that could overlap with your market, we’ll tell you before it becomes a problem.

items.q: Whose name goes on the report?
items.a: Set on the first mandate. Both models exist: delivered under your name with Factum as the engine, or co-delivered.

items.q: Can you run only part of the scope?
items.a: The eleven-discipline pass is fixed, because the value sits in the reconciliation between disciplines. What varies is the depth of the write-up.
Exclusivity is possible in a defined lane, and it is a real commitment when we make it.

sections.title: Your rights

If you are not satisfied, you can complain to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, the Dutch data protection authority.
